idea.body: Volume is the amount of space a solid takes up on the inside, measured in cubic units. Surface area is the total area of every face on the outside. A rover's battery pack is a rectangular box 4 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide, and 2 centimeters tall. Its volume is 4 times 3 times 2, which is 24 cubic centimeters. Its surface area adds up all six faces. Two faces are 4 by 3, two are 4 by 2, and two are 3 by 2. That adds to 24 plus 16 plus 12, which is 52 square centimeters. A cube is a rectangular prism where every side is the same length, so its volume is that length multiplied by itself three times.

figure.alt: A rover's battery pack, a rectangular prism 4 by 3 by 2 centimeters.

workedExample.prompt: A 3D printer's storage box is a rectangular prism 6 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide, and 3 centimeters tall. Find its volume and its surface area.
steps: Volume is length times width times height: 6 x 4 x 3 = 72 cubic centimeters.
Surface area adds up all six faces: two of 6 by 4, two of 6 by 3, and two of 4 by 3.
Those face areas are 24, 18 and 12, each counted twice: 24 + 24 + 18 + 18 + 12 + 12 = 108.
The surface area is 108 square centimeters.

figure.alt: A 3D printer's storage box, a rectangular prism 6 by 4 by 3 centimeters.

ways.name: The formula, three pairs of faces
ways.when: Use this any time you know all three edge lengths of a rectangular prism.
steps: A storage box is a rectangular prism 6 by 4 by 3 centimeters.
Volume is length times width times height: 6 times 4 times 3 is 72.
Surface area adds up all six faces, in three matching pairs.
The face areas are 24, 18 and 12, each counted twice: that totals 108.
ways.example: A box is a rectangular prism 6 by 4 by 3 centimeters. Find its volume and surface area.
ways.trap: Counting each face only once instead of doubling every one of the three pairs.

figure.alt: A rectangular prism 6 by 4 by 3 centimeters, drawn with hidden edges dashed.

ways.name: The net unfolded
ways.when: Use this when you want to see all six faces laid flat instead of grouping them into pairs.
steps: A prism 5 by 3 by 2 centimeters unfolds into six flat rectangles.
Two faces are 5 by 3, two are 5 by 2, and two are 3 by 2.
Find each flat rectangle's area: 15, 15, 10, 10, 6 and 6.
Add all six areas together for the total surface area.
15 plus 15 plus 10 plus 10 plus 6 plus 6 is 62.
ways.example: A prism 5 by 3 by 2 centimeters is unfolded into its six faces. Find the surface area.
ways.trap: Drawing or counting only some of the six faces in the unfolded net.

figure.alt: A rectangular prism 5 by 3 by 2 centimeters unfolded into its six flat faces, each labelled with its own area.

ways.name: Count layers of unit cubes
ways.when: Use this to picture volume as stacked layers instead of one multiplication.
steps: A box is 4 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide, and 5 centimeters tall.
The base layer holds 4 times 3, which is 12 unit cubes.
The box is 5 layers tall, so stack that base layer 5 times.
12 cubes per layer times 5 layers is 60 cubes in total.
ways.example: A box is 4 by 3 centimeters at the base and 5 centimeters tall. Find its volume in unit cubes.
ways.trap: Multiplying only two of the three dimensions and forgetting to stack the layers.

figure.alt: A base layer of 12 unit cubes, 3 by 4, stacked 5 layers high, showing the volume of the full box.

frames.caption: Box is 4 by 3 at the base.

ways.name: The cube shortcut
ways.when: Use this only when every edge of the solid is the same length.
steps: A storage cube has 5 centimeter sides.
A cube's surface area is 6 times one face's area, since every face matches.
One face is 5 times 5, which is 25 square centimeters.
6 times 25 is 150.
ways.example: A storage cube has 5 centimeter sides. Find its surface area.
ways.trap: Forgetting to multiply by 6 faces after finding one face's area.
